t: CAPRI
Boat tour to view the Faraglioni Rocks and the Blue Grotto

The Faraglioni Rock formations of Capri tower above the surface of the sea. The closest stack to the shore is called Stella. The second - the middle stack - Faraglioni di Mezzo, has the famous archway. The third tower is known as the Faraglioni di Fuori. The Blue Grotto allows beautiful blue sunlight to reflect through the water for a spectacular show. Homes are built high on the cliffs.

t: The UMBRIAN HILLS and ASSISI

Umbria is a region in central Italy. It is characterized by hills, mountains, valleys and historical towns, such as Assisi, a World Heritage Site. Religious pilgrims have come to Assisi for centuries to visit the Basilica of San Francisco, where St. Francis is buried. Saint Francis founded the Franciscan religious order in Assisi in 1208. Assisi is also the home of the Basilica of Santa Chiara, where the tomb of St. Clare, the founder of the Sisters of the Poor, is located.
The Basilica of Maria Degli Angeli is located on the Umbrian plains near Assisi. Built between 1569 and 1679, it enclosed the PORZIUNCULAI (little church), the most sacred place for the Franciscans.

t: VENICE

Venice is located in northeastern Italy. It is situated on a group of 118 small islands that are separated by canals and linked by over 400 bridges. The islands are located in the shallow Venetian Lagoon where approximately 55,000 people live. There are about 500,000 in greater Venice, counting the mainland. In 1987, Venice and its Lagoon were designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
A private motor launch takes us on a canal cruise to St. Mark's Square, where we view the Byzantine Basilica, Bridge of Signs and the Doges' Palace.

t: ROME THE COLISEUM

The Coliseum, also known as the Flavian Amphitheater, is in the center of Rome. It is oval in shape and built of Travertine limestone, tuff, and brick-faced concrete. It could hold 50,000 spectators. Construction began in 72 AD and was completed in 80 AD. It was a gift to the Roman people by the Flavian emperors for entertainment including gladiatorial combats and wild animal fights.
VATICAN CITY ST. PETER'S BASILICA

Designed by Bramante, Michelangelo, Maderno, and Bernini, it is the most renowned work of Renaissance architecture and the largest church in the world. Construction was started by Pope Julius II in 1506 AD and completed in 1615 AD under Paul V. It is designed as a three-aisled Latin cross with a dome at the crossing, directly above the high altar, which covers the shrine of St. Peter.

t: Vatican City - Sistine Chapel

The Sistine Chapel is located in the Apostolic Palace, the official residence of the Pope. The chapel takes its name from Pope Sixtus IV, who restored it between 1477 and 1480. It is a place of both religious and functionary papal activities, including the papal conclave, the process by which a new pope is selected. Its fame lies in the many frescos that decorate the interior - most notably the ceiling of The Last Judgment by Michelangelo.

Built on top of an extinct volcano, Edinburgh Castle is a historic fortress which dominates the skyline of Edinburgh, the capital of Scotland, from its position on the Castle Rock. There has been a royal castle on the rock since the reign of David I in the 12th century. By the 17th century it was principally used as a military barracks and prison. The castle was the birthplace of King James VI, only child of Mary Queen of Scots and was witness to many defining events in Scottish history and in the lives of Scottish monarchs.

STONE OF SCONE, also known as the STONE OF DESTINY (or CORONATION STONE) is an oblong block of red sandstone. Legends of its origins date back to biblical times. A descendant of King Gathelus brought the Stone to Ireland and was crowned on it as king of Ireland. From Ireland, the Stone moved with the invading Scots to its home in Scone. The Stone remained in Scone until it was forcibly removed by English King Edward in 1296 and taken to Westminster Abbey. Every English monarch since 1296 has sat on the Stone for their coronation. On Christmas Day in 1950, the Stone was famously abducted from Westminster by a group of Glasgow students who brought it back to Scotland. The Stone was returned by the Stone-nappers the following April. In 1996, the Stone was returned to Scotland where it is kept today. THE CORONATION CHAIR was made to house the stone in 1301 and it was first used at the coronation of Edward II, and thereafter to crown all kings and queens of England.

t: We drove from Edinburgh to Stirling, Scotland where we toured Stirling Castle.

Stirling Castle is one of the most important castles in Great Britain. The castle was built in early 12th century, on a hill of volcanic rock. Its other buildings were added from the period 1490-1600. At the castle's heart is the Inner Close, a square formed by the King's Old Building, Great Hall, Royal Palace, Royal Chapel, and the gardens. The castle is surrounded by a heavy defense of walls, towers, gates, and artillery. It was very much a palace as well as a fortress. Several Scottish Kings and Queens have been crowned here including Mary Queen of Scots, in 1542. Many others were born or died here.
STIRLING CASTLE

THE GREAT HALL - Built for James IV around 1503, is the largest banqueting hall in Scotland. There are five ornate fireplaces, spiral stairways and a hammer- beam roof constructed from around 350 oak trees. In 1594, James VI held a banquet for the baptism of his son, Prince Henry. The fish course was served from a model wooden ship complete with firing cannons.

CASTLE MENZIES - A spectacular 16th century Scottish castle, restored in the 20th century. It is a Renaissance example of the transition from earlier rugged fortresses to later mansion houses. Because it has been restored from a ruin, it is much less furnished and decorated. The ancestral seat of the Clan Menzies, the castle had been occupied by the same family for 400 years and is currently owned by the Menzies Clan Society. It is located to the west of the small village of Weem, near Aberfeldy.

While at the Castle, we were entertained by Alan Brown in his production of "This is Scotland...and you're welcome to it." The show is an irreverent look and listen in words and music of Scotland, with a particular emphasis on Highland Perthshire.

t: FOLLOWING OUR BOAT TOUR WE VISITED THE ANNE FRANK HAUS

Annelies Marie "Anne" Frank was a German-Dutch girl of Jewish origin. During WW II, Anne and her family were German refugees to Amsterdam from the city of Frankfurt. For over two years, Anne Frank and her family hid in the annex of the building at Prinsengracht 263 where Anne's father Otto Frank, worked. She gained fame posthumously with the publication of The Diary of a Young Girl, in which she documents her life in hiding from 1942 to 1944, during the German occupation of the Netherlands in World War II. She died at the Bergen-Belsen Concentration Camp, probably of typhus, in 1945 at the age of 15, just two months before the War ended.

Situated on the banks of the river Neckar, HEIDELBERG is one of Germany's most beautiful towns. For centuries it was a center of political power and cultural life. In 1386, Germany's first university was established here. HEIDELBERG PALACE was built during the 17th century. HEIDELBERG CASTLE ruins are among the most important Renaissance structures north of the Alps. The castle is several buildings clustered around a courtyard, each representing different styles of German architecture. t: HEIDELBERG

While in medieval Old Town, we also walked the famous Old Bridge (Karl Theodor Bridge). The bridge crosses the NECKAR RIVER connecting the OLD CITY with the eastern section. The twin towers were once part of the city wall and contained dungeons. Heidelberg's oldest bridge, it is an architecturally impressive landmark decorated with an imperious gateway, detailed sculptures, and a curious monkey holding a mirror. The monkey sculpture welcomed all to Heidelberg and was meant to remind those who crossed the bridge to look back and remember where they had come from. Local legend has it that rubbing the mirror brings good luck, rubbing the fingers ensures a return to Heidelberg, and rubbing the little bronze-cast mice brings fertility.

t: CARIBBEAN CRUISE JULY 8 - JULY 13, 2017 - TAMPA FLORIDA, KEY WEST FLORIDA, FUN DAY AT SEA, COZUMEL MEXICO, FUN DAY AT SEA

The Frenches planned a FAMILY CRUISE for July of 2017. After locating the best cruise for all of our schedules (not easy to do), departure ports and itineraries, we selected a CARNIVAL PARADISE CRUISE, round trip from Tampa. Since we live in the Tampa area, this was a great place to meet and then depart for our trip. We also hoped that the "KIDS" could extend their time in Florida and stay with us for a few days. The kids decided to surprise "Pops" and "Lollie" by paying for our cruise to celebrate our upcoming July 29, 2017, 50th Wedding Anniversary. Needless to say we were more than thrilled with their generous gift. Obviously, we raised three thoughtful sons who together with their wonderful families have enriched our already blessed lives. We will always remember their wonderful surprise!
ART & GIN'S 50TH ANNIVERSARY CELEBRATION
TAMPA, FLORIDA

SATURDAY, JULY 8: We board the Carnival Paradise at noon in Tampa, Florida and settle into our rooms. After lunch in the Paris Dining Room, we spend the rest of the day exploring the ship, relaxing by the pool with a beverage, attending the Sail Away Party on the Lido Deck, and enjoying dinner in the Destiny Dining Room.
In the evening, we attend the Welcome Aboard Show in the Normandie Lounge, where our Cruise Director shared highlights of the cruise. We then were entertained with a Playlist Productions show.

Later in the evening, we checked out the Majestic Casino, enjoyed a comedy act in the Punchliner Comedy Club that is located in the Queen Mary Lounge, and stopped in at the American Piano Bar before heading back to our rooms. Brad, on the other hand, spent most late, late nights at the Rex Nightclub.

SUNDAY, JULY 9: After a morning of leisure, we arrive in Key West, Florida. While in Key West, we explore the historic streets, visit the shops, had lunch at Sloppy Joe's Restaurant/Bar, and then dessert at the Key West Lime Shoppe. We saw Hemingway's 6-toed cats, roaming chickens and the Southernmost Point of the continental United States. Bryan, Mary, Maddy and Katie paid a visit to the Key West Butterfly and Nature Conservatory.

After dinner on the ship, we went to the Captain's Toast Celebration in the lobby, and then headed to the Punchliner Comedy Club for a performance by a stand-up comedian. Later in the evening, we visited the Majestic Casino and the Leonardo Bar for karaoke. After a few beverages for courage, "Lollie" was sung to by Bryan during his debut karaoke performance.
FUN DAY AT SEA

MONDAY, JULY 10: This was our first full day to relax, enjoy the sun, explore more of the ship, and participate in some of the on-board activities. Art and Gin discovered the Rotterdam Martini Bar which became a favorite place for a pre-dinner cocktail. At times we were blessed with the company of Brad, Eric, and Carol. After dinner, we went to the evening Production: "80's Pop to the Max". After the show, we spent some time watching karaoke in the Leonardo Bar and then off to the Piano Bar for a late night drink.
COZUMEL, MEXICO

TUESDAY, JULY 11: We arrive in Cozumel at 8:00 AM and after breakfast, we set off to explore Cozumel. Gin and Art spend the day at the shops and relaxing at Pancho's Backyard Waterfront Restaurant for drinks and appetizers. Bryan, Mary, Katie and Daryn explore the Island of Cozumel by Jeep, including a stop at the San Gervasio Mayan Site to view the ruins. Carol, Eric, Andrew, Brad and Maddy head out for an excursion: "All Inclusive Isla Pasion by Twister", an adrenaline-rushing boat ride with high speed maneuvers to the private island of Isla Pasion. Here, amenities included beach chairs, hammocks, and soaking up the sun; all served with a Mayan lunch and domestic open bar. On return to Cozumel, the "Gang of Five" went to one of the local beach bars for a beverage and snacks. We all met up for dinner and evening activities including the Love and Marriage Show in the Normandie Lounge and a Lido Deck Party.

We saw Hemingway's 6-toed cats, roaming chickens and the Southernmost Point of the continental United States. We then watched as Brad launched his Drone for some spectacular views of Key West and the surrounding waters. Unfortunately, "Dronie" met up with a palm tree and became forever disabled. To forget the accident, we headed to a water front bar. After dinner on the ship, we went to the evening production of "80's Pop to the Max", and headed to the Punchliner Comedy Club.
HAVANA, CUBA

WEDNESDAY, APRIL 10: We disembark our ship and meet up with our Excursion Guide who narrates as we explore historic Havana Cuba. A short boat ride across the bay takes us past the statue of El Cristo, an impressive 55-foot-tall statue of Christ sculpted in Italian Marble. We begin our walking tour through the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Old Havana, exploring the vibrant colors and people of this 16th century part of the city. Here, there are four main squares or plazas each offering its own unique characteristics, vendors, street performers and musicians. These include: Plaza de San Francisco de Asis (St. Francis of Assisi Square), Plaza de Armas, Plaza de la Catedral and Plaza Vieja.

Our first stop is Plaza de San Francisco de Asis which is a short distance from the docks. This Plaza, founded on June 2, 1628, is one of the oldest squares in Havana. Here we have time to see The Basilica of St. Francis of Assisi and numerous other historic buildings. Next, we visited Plaza de Armas with its many historic buildings, wooden street and street performers. The main highlight of this Plaza is the park with its beautiful palm trees and marble statues. Our Excursion Director then took us to visit the Fortaleza de San Carlos de la Cabana (Fort of St. Charles) complex that served in the defense of Old Havana back in the days of pirates and privateers. While here, we also saw a demonstration of cigar making. Our way back to Old Havana took us past El Capitolio (the National Capitol Building) and Obispo Street, in Central Park, the most populous street in Old Havana, with all of its vintage cars on display.
HAVANA, CUBA (Narrative continued)

We enjoyed lunch at a local restaurant and then were entertained by the Retazos Dance Company. This performance was a part of our requirement to participate in a group people-to-people exchange for authorized travel to Cuba. This contemporary dance group is one of the most admired dance companies in Latin America. In the afternoon, we continued our tour by bus through Old Havana's streets and neighborhoods where we viewed local Cubans, their homes, shops, schools and vintage cars. As a part of our bus tour, we had photo opportunities at Plaza de La Catedral (Cathedral Square). Following the construction of the Cathedral in 1727, it became the site of some of the city's grandest mansions and numerous restaurants.

Our tour did not have time to visit Plaza Vieja, also known as Old Town Square. Here, Colonial buildings allowed residents in the early 16th century, a view of public demonstrations such as bullfights, processions and even executions. Today, the Square has many restaurants and bars. Our tour ended back at our ship. After dinner, we joined other cruise guests at the Piano Bar.
COZUMEL, MEXICO

THURSDAY, APRIL 11: We arrive in Cozumel at noon; and after breakfast and relaxation, we set off to explore Cozumel. Gin and Art spend the day at the shops and relaxing at Pancho's Backyard Waterfront Restaurant for drinks and appetizers. Carol, Eric, Andrew and Brad head out for an excursion: "All Inclusive Isla Pasion by Twister", an adrenaline-rushing boat ride with high speed maneuvers to the private island of Isla Pasion. Here, amenities included beach chairs, hammocks, and soaking up the sun; all served with a Mayan lunch and domestic open bar. On return to Cozumel, the "Gang of Four" went to one of the local beach bars for a beverage and snacks. We all met up for dinner and evening activities including Karaoke and a Deck Party.

He was the initiator of the Cuban wars of independence and Father of the Homeland. In 1955, his statue replaced that of the unpopular Spanish King Fernando VII, which now stands in the loggia of the Palacio de los Capitanes Generales. Tacon Street on the west side of the square is of parquet of wood brick. Originally the Governor's home was located in Plaza de Armas. We were unable to visit PLAZA VIEJA (OLD SQUARE) during our tour, but our Excursions Director shared interesting facts about this historic Square. The 16th century PLAZA VIEJA has always been a residential rather than a military, religious, or administrative space. It is surrounded by elegant colonial residences, combined with a few early 20th century art nouveau buildings. Colonial buildings in the early 16th century, afforded residents a view of public demonstrations such as bullfights, processions, and executions. In the past, the Plaza has been an open-air food market, a park, an amphitheater, and a car park. Today, many of the residences around the square are now restored with housing on the top floors and commercial establishments on the lower levels. The square is one of the most beautiful with many restaurants and bars.

t: LA SAGRADA FAMILIA

La Sagrada Familia, meaning Holy Family, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The original architect, Francisco de Paula del Villar, had a plan for a Gothic revival church. Construction began in 1882 and Antoni Gaudi became involved in 1883. La Sagrada Familia was envisioned by Gaudi with a total of 18 towers; twelve dedicated to the Apostles, the others to the Four Evangelists, the Virgin Mary and Christ. At the time of Gaudi's death in 1926, less than a quarter of it was complete. It has a completion date of 2026, the centennial of Gaudi's death. The Crypt, the oldest part of the Basilica, is where Gaudi was buried. In November, 2010, La Sagrada Familia was consecrated and proclaimed a minor basilica by Pope Benedict XVI.

t: CRETE - Knossos Palace

Crete is home to an array of sights, monuments and archeological wonders. It was the cradle of the Mediterranean's early Bronze Age. Our first stop was its capital Knossos and the famous Minoan Palace, with 1,300 rooms and corridors. According to Greek mythology, it was the home of King Minos. Originally constructed in 1900 B.C, it was destroyed and rebuilt before its final destruction in 1400 B.C. In 1878, a merchant discovered the ruins. Twenty-five years later, Sir Arthur Evans unearthed and controversially restored much of what is here today.

Our guide took us to the West Court, a ceremonial center. Once inside the palace we viewed the Charging Bull Fresco and the Throne Room. Opposite the throne is a fresco depicting griffins, the beast with an eagle's head and lion's body which is a symbol of royal and divine power.

t: MYKONOS GREECE

We returned to Mykonos for a guided walking tour. Mykonos is a picturesque town with tiny streets, white houses and red roofed churches. It is one of Greece's most expensive islands after becoming a home to the jet set. We saw windmills dotting the landscape, to remind us that the island was once known for its agriculture. We viewed Little Venice famous for its narrow rows of colored fishing houses that sit at the edge of the sea. Originally the homes belonged to rich merchants. Little Venice is a hub of activity with shops and restaurants. We saw Paraportiani Church, which is actually five churches; four comprise the base and the fifth is built as the dome. After the tour, we walked the streets on our own past the many shops, boutiques and had lunch.
